abstract: Deep learning-based text to speech (TTS) is used in various situations, and the sound quality is close to that of humans. We previously developed a news-specific deep learning-based TTS (DL-TTS) system and implemented it with our AI news anchor for live broadcast programs and automatic news-speech distribution services. We also developed our DL-TTS system for the control of speaking style and speech rate, pitch, intonation, and volume to facilitate the creation of various programs. More specifically, this method enables the changing of specific speaking styles, such as news style, which mimics the style of news reporters, and conversation style. The purpose of creating this system was to eliminate the discomfort due to differences in speech and speaking styles. Controlling speaking style is important in news speech because a mismatched speaking style does not appropriately convey news articles. For this study, we conducted an evaluation experiment on the conveying of simple news articles for language learners regarding speaking-style control and found appropriate speaking styles for automatically generated news speech. We conducted another evaluation experiment on whether synthetic speech generated from our system for “easy news” for Japanese language learners can help people understand the news in Japanese. We also discuss practical applications of our system. Our news-specific deep neural network-based TTS system was found to effectively provide news services to broadcast stations. In the future, we will consider various use cases of flexible production by using a cloud system. The coronavirus pandemic has forced broadcasters to adopt new working styles. Thus, we will explore a new production system, such as a cloud-based system, for news-speech automation for this new normal.

authors.bio: Kiyoshi Kurihara received BE and ME degrees in electronics and communications from Meiji University, Tokyo, Japan, in 2004 and 2006, respectively. After his graduation, he joined NHK (Japan Broadcasting Corporation), Tokyo, where he was a master control and radio studio engineer in a broadcasting station. He joined the Science and Technology Research Laboratories (STRL) in 2016. He joined the Development and Strategy Center in 2020. His current interest includes speech synthesis for broadcast.
authors.name: Kiyoshi Kurihara

authors.bio: Nobumasa Seiyama received BE and ME degrees in electrical engineering from Waseda University, Tokyo, Japan, in 1987 and 1989, respectively. He joined NHK in 1989. Since then, he has worked with the Science and Technology Research Laboratories, engaging in speech signal processing, voice conversion, speech synthesis, and development of a high-quality speech rate conversion system for the elderly. He was with NHK Engineering Services, Inc., from 2007 to 2010.
authors.name: Nobumasa Seiyama

authors.bio: Tadashi Kumano is a principal research engineer with the Science and Technology Research Laboratories NHK. He joined NHK STRL after getting his master’s degree in computer science from the Graduate School of Information Science and Engi?neering, Tokyo Institute of Technology, Tokyo, in 1995. He was also a member of the Advanced Telecommunication Research (ATR) Institute International Spoken Language Translation Laboratories from 2000 to 2004. He has been engaged in the research of natural language processing and machine translation, and recently became interested in spoken language generation such as computer-producing voice commentaries for sports programs.
authors.name: Tadashi Kumano

authors.bio: Takashi Fukaya is a senior manager with the Development and Strategy Center News Department. After graduating from Kyushu Institute of Design, Fukuoka, Japan, he joined NHK in 1992. While with the NHK Science and Technical Research Laboratories, he conducted research on human interaction and released “Invisible Light” and “Virtual Scope.” He has also collaborated with media artist Toshio IWAI to present “Morphovision” at SIGGRAPH 2006 and ARS Electronica 2006. Currently, he has been engaged in NHK News website and application development work. He received a PhD degree in design from the Kyushu Institute of Design.
authors.name: Takashi Fukaya

authors.bio: Kazunari Saito is the technical director of the Development and Strategy Center News Department. After graduating from Keio University, Tokyo, Japan, he joined NHK in 2002. After working on data broadcasting and interactive con?tent development, he focused on the NHK News website and application development. He is currently active as a key member of the cloud infrastructure design team.
authors.name: Kazunari Saito

authors.bio: Satoshi Suzuki is a CG super?visor, an expert in the field of CG for over 20 years. He joined NHK in 1997 and worked at their Osaka Broadcasting Station. Since 2001, he has been with the Broadcast Engineering department, where he has been engaged in developing NHK election systems and CG production systems. More recently, he has been working as a CG supervisor mainly to develop the “big data visualization system.”
authors.name: Satoshi Suzuki
